deep.reconstruction:
Caveat: the page is extremely faint. Only the layout, a few symbols and the general shape of the formulas can be made out. Everything below is a structural reconstruction, not a reading.

(0) Top lines. The first four or five lines of Kurrent closely match, line by line, the text of the previous page (71r): 'keine Lösung mehr hat, während es für jeden Werth von a/b(?), der über dieser Grenze liegt, zwei Werthe von m, also zwei Lösungen der Aufgabe giebt. Es ist anzunehmen, daß nur der kleinere der beiden Werthe von m einem wirklichen Minimum entspricht.' At least one of these lines is struck through. Two explanations fit: (a) a draft of the same passage, cancelled here and recopied on 71r; or (b) bleed-through of 71r showing on the verso. The image cannot decide between them; (a) is suggested by the visible strike-through and the leftward-looking slant is inconclusive.

(1) Context. The bundle 'R.Minimal' holds the material behind Riemann's 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', edited by Hattendorff in 1867. The page belongs to one of the worked examples in which the minimal surface is bounded by straight lines. There the coordinates are given by Weierstrass/Riemann-type integrals whose integrand contains the square root of a quartic in the uniformizing variable s.

(2) A short displayed relation, then a line of text ending in '... = 0', then a further short relation. It is probably the normalisation or symmetry condition fixing the constants, e.g. a relation between the parameter m and a constant in the quartic. It is unreadable.

(3) A line mentioning 'X, Y, Z'. It is followed by three displayed integrals of the form (reconstruction mine):
 X = (c/(2√k)) ∫_0^s ds/√(1 − p s² + q s⁴),
 Y = (c/(2√k)) ∫ ds/√(1 − p s² + q s⁴) · (γ − 1/γ),
 Z = (c/(2√k)) ∫ ds/√(1 − p s² + q s⁴) · (γ' − 1/γ').
Here the factors in parentheses are built from a quantity and its reciprocal. This is the familiar shape of the components (1−g²)f, i(1+g²)f, 2gf of a Weierstrass representation, written with a Gauss-map variable and its inverse. The coordinates are thus elliptic integrals.

(4) Text, then 'a und b ...' (probably 'a und b sind gegeben durch'), then two displayed definite integrals:
 a = (c/(2√k)) ∫_0^1(?) ds/√(...) · (γ + 1/γ),
 b = (c/(2√k)) ∫_0^∞(?) ds/√(...) · (√.../γ + √.../γ).
These express the given boundary data (distance or offset between the bounding lines) as complete elliptic integrals, i.e. periods of the representation along the boundary segments.

(5) A sentence: 'In diesem besonderen Fall, daß beide ... einander gleich sind, ... = 0 ... und erhält ... zur Bestimmung ... die transcendente Gleichung'. In the symmetric special case one parameter vanishes. The ratio of the two given lengths is then expressed by one equation:
 a/b (or similar) = ∫_0^{...} ds/√(...) (...).
This is a single transcendental equation for the remaining parameter m.

(6) Closing paragraph, five or more faint lines, unreadable. Judging from the matching text, it discusses that this equation has no solution below a critical value of the ratio and two solutions above it. Only the smaller m is presumed to give a true minimum.

Right margin: scattered illegible notes, perhaps auxiliary numbers or a word such as 'für ...'.
errors: Cannot assess the correctness of individual steps: the formulas are too faint to read their exact coefficients, limits or the radicands of the quartic roots.

The claim that only the smaller of the two m-values gives a genuine minimum is stated (on the matching text) as a presumption ('Es ist anzunehmen'), not proved. This is an honest, unjustified-but-flagged step, and it is consistent with later stability theory: of two solution branches, typically one is unstable.

results.what: Representation of a minimal surface bounded by straight lines through elliptic integrals (quartic square root) in the coordinates X, Y, Z
results.modern_name: Weierstrass–Enneper representation; Riemann–Schwarz solution of Plateau problems for polygonal boundaries
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published posthumously 1867 by Hattendorff), Weierstrass (1866), Schwarz (1865, skew quadrilateral)

results.what: Expressing the given boundary lengths a, b as complete elliptic integrals (period conditions) and reducing the symmetric case to one transcendental equation for the parameter m
results.modern_name: Period problem / parameter determination for minimal surfaces with polygonal boundary

results.what: Observation that the parameter equation has no solution below a threshold and two above it, with only the smaller root presumed to be a true minimum
results.modern_name: Non-uniqueness / fold bifurcation of solutions to a Plateau problem; stability of minimal surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's memoir (examples section); stability theory later (Schwarz 1872 onward)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a faint draft or bleed-through of material corresponding to the published (1867) Riemann/Hattendorff memoir on minimal surfaces. It covers elliptic-integral parametrisation of a polygon-bounded minimal surface, period conditions, and a symmetric special case with two solutions. Nothing beyond what is already attributed to Riemann can be read.

checkable.asserts: The Weierstrass data (1-g^2, i(1+g^2), 2g) are isotropic (sum of squares is 0), so the integrals of the type X, Y, Z give a conformal minimal immersion.
The sum of |components|^2 equals 2(1+|g|^2)^2, the metric factor of the representation; the result should simplify to 0.
Sanity check of the degenerate case: as the quartic radicand 1 - p s^2 + q s^4 degenerates to (1-s^2)^2 or 1-s^2, the integrals reduce to elementary functions.

transcription_corrections: The first 4-5 lines (one partly struck through) are not illegible noise. They correspond closely to the text given for the previous page: 'keine Lösung (Auflösung?) mehr hat, während es für jeden Werth von a/b(?), der über dieser Grenze liegt, zwei Werthe von m, also zwei Lösungen der Aufgabe giebt. Es ist anzunehmen, daß nur der kleinere der beiden Werthe von m einem wirklichen Minimum entspricht.' Either this is a cancelled draft of that passage or bleed-through from 71r.
The X integral visibly has limits 0 to s and a radicand of quartic type (roughly √(1 − ... s² + ... s⁴)), not just '√…'.
The b formula's bracket contains two fractions with square roots in the numerators (shape (√…/γ + √…/γ)), as the machine transcription roughly indicates.

The text before the final displayed formula appears to read 'In diesem besonderen Fall, daß beide ... einander gleich sind, ... = 0 ... erhält ... die transcendente Gleichung'. This marks a symmetric special case reducing to one equation for m.
